comment: Such an awesome guy. He wants you to think he's scary but you'll quickly realize he's not. He's so knowledgeable and supportive. Jump on the opportunity to take a class with Mullen.

Very funny teacher who is extremely passionate about journalism. The class is very entertaining. Weekly news quizzes that most people did poorly on. The class atmosphere was lowkey stressful. In hindsight, it was a really good class, but I dreaded going every day.

STUPID CURRENT EVENTS QUIZ EVERY SINGLE WEEK TANK MY GRADE. other than that the class was light but the weekly current events quizzes took years off my llifespan and my GPA lokwy don't  take this class unless you enjoy memorizing the news very single week. tom is also kinda scary and mean but like i like him

Mullen is amazing. Funny, sarcastic guy. He can sometimes be tough on you but it's because he wants to make you better. Loved this FYS, the material was so interesting and there were lots of real world examples of concepts taught in class. The news quizzes were hard at the start but you adjust quickly. If you get the chance, take a class with him.

His interactions with students were often unforgiving and disrespectful. There were several instances where it felt like the instructor was not interested in helping students succeed. Feedback was delivered in a harsh and dismissive manner, which was discouraging rather than motivating. Constructive criticism should be provided in a supportive way.
He's really funny but also passionate about everything he teaches. If you try you will do well in his class.

Mullen was an amazing professor. True UR legend. Even if you don't major in journalism, he's a professor you want to have. Blasted "Welcome to the Jungle" on day 1; makes class fun like that. Understands first years well and taught me a lot about news and the importance of journalism for a democracy. Very funny and real with world issues. Good FYS.

Very interesting class, definitely take it. News quizzes once a week, so you will need to read the New York Times daily  You write two news reports and take two tests, tests are not difficult as long as you study. Dr. Mullen seems intimidating, but cares about students. Great man and professor. Great feedback on assignments, and available to help.

Mullen was a great professor that always managed to keep me engaged. The class was very interesting and showed me a new side of journalism. Had to read three books but they are quick. And most of the writing topics are very broad so it is easier to write.

Prof Mullen is my favorite so far! He was super accessible outside of class and gave good feedback. If instructions were ever unclear, he was always willing to talk and clarify. Lectures were informative and engaging. The more you participate, the better he will like you. He will give you edits before a final draft if you ask!

Mullen is easily one of the best professors on campus. A balanced amount of coursework, very accessible and knowledgeable. He may be intimidating at first, but he cares about his students so much. His classes are very manageable -- anyone who complains about him probably either don't show up or doesn't do any work.

Mullen was my FYS prof and my advisor and I would say he screwed me in both. According to my own experience and my classmates, he seemed to have it out for me from day one and was useless as an advisor. He gives confusing edits on your articles and then grades harshly when you don't understand what to fix. As an advisor he has given me zero advice

Professor Mullen is very hot and cold. He can be very kind at times but very abrasive and arrogant at other times. He does know a lot about journalism and talks a lot about his previous jobs. He gave a lot of reading assignments and the books were very interesting. At times, his expectations were unclear and he was very harsh. He often cold calls.

Mullen will always have your back. He might seem intimidating, but he really cares and has devoted himself to helping students become better writers and journalists. Highly recommend taking one of his classes, even if you arent a journalism major/minor. You will become a much better writer because of it.

Amazing lectures, really funny professor. Wants to seem like a mean professor, but he's really nice. There are weekly quizzes based on current events. You'll have to read a book per week. Midterm and Final were super easy (multiple choice) based on movies and books that you'll see and read for the class. Don't be absent or use your phone in class

Mullen attempts to scare you the first day of class, but stick it out and it will be worth it. He wants to challenge his students, but not in an unreasonable way. He expects you to show up to class, participate, and get the homework in on time. His grading criteria are clear, and even if you start off terribly, by the end you will see improvement.

He is an incredibly hard grader on the news stories. You have to do assigned readings or else you will get called on and picked apart. Easy to get on his bad side. Expects that you become a journalist by taking this course.

he is really hard for me, though I don't know others. he is a very tough grader towards news writing, I got bad grades on those. And final project is time-consuming and frustrating. news quiz is also not easy for me I always got a 5 or 6 on them. I really love journalism, but i just didn't get good grades.

Dr. Mullen was really cool. I took his news media and society course over the summer and learned quite a bit in just 5 weeks. The nature of summer classes can make the course seem daunting but Dr. Mullen did an outstanding job of organizing the class to make students feel comfortable with the heavy course load. A very good experience overall.

Mullen is great - he can come off rude at first but its just his humor. He always wants to help, inside and outside the classroom. Very lenient on tests & projects, only tough on the news-style essays (only 2) He LOVES  when you participate in class. Seems like a lot of reading but you can just skim. Very interesting topics too - I would take again

Mr. Mullen is an amazing teacher. He knows to be funny and engaging in class and gets you single handedly into noticing the 'culture' by awarding class credits for it! The news quizzes everyday was annoying at first, but it becomes a daily routine soon and you won't even notice it.

Professor Mullen was a great choice for FYS.  Weekly news quizzes are supposed to make you keep up with the NYT, but they're pretty easy to get around.  Tests are minimal and easy and assignments are clear and not very intense.  The big drawback is that the material gets dry at times, and you really do have to show up to every class.

I took him for my FYS. I did not do well at all. His attention to detail is obsessive and his nit pickiness with papers is incredibly frustrating. The actual content is interesting and those tests are easy. However, he expects you to become a journalist overnight the second you walk into his class: bloody stupid ITS AN FYS! We didn't have a choice!

Mullen is the best. He's charismatic and knows what he's talking about. If you're not paying attention or don't raise your hand, he might call you out (but he's funny and respectful about it). He jokes around a lot which makes it fun and easy to understand the material. If you do the assignments, the tests are a breeze. He's an awesome teacher!

Best professor I've had at UR. Single handedly got me interested in journalism. Be on the ball in class, otherwise he will call you out. Not a cake walk by any means, but if you put forth an effort you will do well.
One of my favorite classes at U of R!

Professor Mullen is a nice guy, but he's a very sassy professor.  He will call you out if you're doing anything that bothers him (ex: eating a pop tart the wrong way).  I did fine in the class, but his attitude was barely tolerable.

TAKE THIS MAN'S CLASS IF YOU'RE AT ALL INTERESTED IN JOURNALISM. My favorite professor at UR so far. Extremely knowledgeable and experienced. Incredibly accessible and helpful. I once called his cell phone on a Sunday and he answered and talked with me for 30 minutes about an assignment. Very funny and engaging. Highly recommend him.

Mullen would be a great substitute host for a late night comedy show.  He’s funny and entertaining and you never know what to expect from day to day. Tests are easy, but news quizzes and papers can be challenging.  A must for anyone that’s remotely interested in Journalism and a solid choice for FYS, with a lot of interesting topics explored.
He is the man!! I always loved going to class and hearing his witty comments. His event quizzes are tough but overall he's awesome!

Professor Mullen is an incredible teacher. He's clear, concise, and keeps his students attention through interwoven stories, lectures, and other media tools. He enjoys seeing people participate in his class, so make sure to speak up about a current event or if you have a question. His current event quizzes are tricky, so study!
Great teacher. Very helpful. Not too much reading and participation is not too big a deal. The tests are rather easy but he is a little tougher on the papers and speeches.

Few in his field can teach more about journalism; he has decades of experience in the field to back it. You will become a better write and learn in his classes, but he makes it clear that you must be a dedicated student. He is funny but sometimes swears. News quizzes are random and puzzling. He always wants to help-cares about his students.

He is a funny guy who's not afraid to speak his mind or occasionally use 'bad' words. He intimidates students who aren't serious in the first few weeks, but he's a nice guy who knows his subject as well as one can--with plenty of experience as a journalist. You will learn a lot in his class and become a better writer. News quizzes are random.

Had him for News, Media, and Society.Great professor. Very good guy and also hilarious. Current event quizzes every week. The tests contain everything you do in class pretty much, not just the books. Gives extra credit opportunities. I'd definitely recommend taking some sort of class with him.

He knows what he is talking about. He rocks in my opinion. My easiest class of the semester, seriously!. I find his grading very fair, and not to tough. If you are not liberal, you will not like this class, seriously. He says what he wants!!
a general good guy who enjoys teaching.  His classes are always entertaining and he is really down to earth.  He is a tough grader but its worth it at the end
Most biased professor I've ever had.

I had Prof. Mullen over the summer and he had to be the coolest professor I'd had all year. Everyone in our class had fun and we ended up learning things I know we didn't expect to learn. On top of that I am now not able to function without reading two newspapers everyday because of him, lol. A great class I definitely recommend it for the summer!

I took news media & society with this guy, and it was great! He's interesting and funny, but also a bit strict- that helps though, because you end up learning a lot. He's great outside of class too... shows personal interest in the success of his students... I look forward to more classes with him.

Great techer, always happy when students participate. Asks for some imput not a robot talker. He gives outlines for test which are very helpful and are exactly what is on the test. Also we read the NY Times every morning so be ready to get up before class to inform him on whats going on in the News.
The man knows his stuff.  He can give you a 2 hour lecture in 30 minutes.  I've never learned more in one class or seen myself progress as much as with copy editing.
news media and society -- very funny
No Comments

Professor Mullen is a great guy. I went into the class and was intimidated for the first couple of days, but after that I realized he really wasn't a very hard teacher, but is just a confident (some might say cocky) guy. He might not be as thorough of a teacher as Mike Spear, but he's more easygoing and more enjoyable to take a class with.

Mullen is a great professor. Class and tests are not difficult, relatively speaking. He is funny, easygoing, and energetic. Do not miss his class though. He never writes down attendance but always seems to know if you miss class, something he despises. But other than that, definitely try to get in his class.

One of my favorite classes. He's really nice, knowledgeable, and his classes are never boring. Work load is average. Just make sure you do the news and book readings but they're easy to understand. If you study the night before for a test, they're not challenging. No final.

Best professor I've ever had.  Super easygoing, hillarious, fun, really knows his stuff.  Workload is heavy, but you'll enjoy it, and he's not one of those profs who gives you unnecesary work for the sake of just giving work. I learned a lot in his class, and I had a blast...even at 8:15.

I can not explain how awful this man is in this limited space, but he is unprofessional, unfriendly, egotistical and a terrible professor.  I would have been better off sleeping through his class than attending.
one of the most student-friendly profs at UR - hands down.
Mullen is one the best professors I ever had.  Prepares you for the field after you get out, class can be hard, but never boring.

Super nice man with a great heart. Very knowledgable in the journalism field. Very fair grader. will like you if you make an effort and get to know him. Awesome and fun, flexible, and has great activties planned for classes

He's a jerk.  He acts like a know it all and makes you feel like crap saying that is how the newsroom is, but he never gives you any positive making you feel lost and you never learn anything.  short man, big ego

This man shoots it to you straight, and you wouldn't want it any other way. He knows the business inside and out and you will leave better prepared for a real job. And he's fun, so you have a great time in class always.
No Comments
Mullen is uber-cool.  He is the only professor I would get up @ 8:15am for.  He will challenge you, insult your writing ability, and make you a better student than you ever thought possible.
